# Fixtures

Two sets of Avro schemas. `raw/` is what Debezium registered; `clean/` is what M4
will register. M5's tests are written against `clean/`.

## raw/

Fetched verbatim from the live registry (`raw.public.*-key/-value`, latest
version) while M3 was running. Ground truth, not authored. Refresh with:

```
make forward
./deid/.venv/bin/python hack/gen-clean-fixtures.py --refresh-raw
```

Two shapes in here are worth knowing before reading any schema-walking code:

- **`before` holds the record definition; `after` is a name reference to it**
  (`["null", "Value"]` where `Value` is a bare string). True for all five tables.
  The project description's "Avro named-type reuse" guardrail states this the
  other way round, so `ddl.py` reads the definition from wherever it actually is
  rather than trusting either spelling.
- **Timestamps are strings, not longs.** The connector runs
  `time.precision.mode=connect`, but a `timestamptz` column is emitted as
  `io.debezium.time.ZonedTimestamp` — an ISO-8601 string — regardless of that
  setting. There is no `timestamp-millis` anywhere in this schema.

## clean/

Generated by `hack/gen-clean-fixtures.py`, which runs M4's already-merged
`deid.ops.build` over `deid/policy/clinic.yml` against `raw/`. So these are
*derived* the same way M4 will derive them, not transcribed from a guess.

They are a faithful stand-in for [DATA-711](https://linear.app/headway/issue/DATA-711)'s
output, not a specification of it. `ddl.py` and `envelope.py` take schema dicts,
so if M4 emits something this does not predict, these files change and the code
does not. Regenerate with `make fixtures`.

The generator refuses to guess: a column whose derivation fails and has no
explicit entry in its `PATCHES` table stops the run. There is one entry.

### The one patch: `patients.date_of_birth`

Deriving this column fails today, so the fixture carries a substituted type:

```
IncompatibleColumnError: public.patients.date_of_birth: op 'generalize' cannot be
applied to a int (org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Date) column: birth_year needs a
date or a timestamp, and this column carries neither
```

`deid/src/deid/avro.py:45` knows the logical-type name
`io.debezium.time.Date`, but `time.precision.mode=connect` makes Debezium emit
`org.apache.kafka.connect.data.Date`. The same file already uses the Connect
spelling for `DECIMAL` (line 54), so the names were half-adopted;
`Time` and `Timestamp` are probably affected too, though no column in this schema
exercises them.

This is an M4 bug, and it is not cosmetic — a rule that refuses its column halts
that topic, so M4 will halt `patients` until it is fixed. Fixing it belongs in
M4's PR, not M5's. Against the name `ops.py` does expect, the same rule derives
`["null", "int"]`, which is what the fixture substitutes.

**The field keeps its original name.** `generalize`'s `to:` is a target *kind*,
not a column name — `postal_code` uses `to: zip3` and `diagnosis_codes` uses
`to: icd10_category`, and neither would sensibly be renamed. M4's own milestone
check ("`dob` is an `int`") reads the same way. If DATA-711 does rename it, only
this fixture changes.

## Notable clean-side shapes

The three that make the sink DDL interesting, all confirmed rather than assumed:

| Column | Clean Avro | Sink |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `claims.billed_amount` | `bytes`, `logicalType: decimal`, `precision: 12`, `scale: 2` | `numeric(12,2)` |
| `claims.diagnosis_codes` | `{"type":"array","items":["null","string"]}` | `text[]` |
| every timestamp | `["null", string + ZonedTimestamp]` | `timestamptz`, **nullable** |

Every timestamp is nullable in the sink even where the source column is
`NOT NULL`: `date_shift` deliberately widens a ZonedTimestamp because a string is
not necessarily an instant (`deid/src/deid/ops.py:744`).

Every primary key is `text`, not `bigint`, because the policy hmacs the ids. That
is the argument for generating DDL from the registry instead of the source's
`information_schema` — the sink's shape is the post-policy shape, and only the
registry knows it.
